art_instructions: From a child’s eye level, show a wide view of the village school entrance: white-washed wall with Mediterranean blue wooden trim, a terracotta-tile roof edge, and two simple wooden porch columns. The blue-trimmed door stands open, and a cooler, darker interior space is visible beyond the threshold to make “inside” clear. Owl (chibi, mottled brown-and-cream, round amber eyes) wears her small green scarf and a tiny cross-body satchel, mid-glide into the doorway with wings half-open, head slightly tilted, and a gentle, eager smile. Place her at right-center, about one-third the door’s height, right foot already past the threshold and left foot lifted, so the action clearly reads “entering.” Set an olive tree on the left and a bougainvillea vine climbing a trellis on the right; a small stone bird bath sits near the steps with a warm puddle of sunlight on the porch. Keep the terracotta roof eave visible above to echo the previous page where she arrived on top, while soft cel-shadows from the columns fall diagonally across the path. Include a tiny butterfly near the flowers for life, but keep it small and secondary. Use the Korean aegyo cute style with flat pastels and clean dark-brown monoline strokes; no text anywhere, and fill the frame edge-to-edge.
